said.setup: Setup happened in the room on Day 1: after the opening talks, everyone installed Claude Code and had Claude interview them to write a context file.
said.skill: In my plenary I demonstrated the resume-tailoring Skill I use myself, then each person built a Skill for a task they repeat. Resume tailoring was one of several starters.
said.agents: Sub-agents and agent fleets were shown on Day 1 as a preview, and the hands-on build stayed with one agent.
said.capstone: For the capstone, people picked a real task, had Claude make mock data, and started building that evening in plan mode.

blocks.name: Welcome and intros
blocks.what: Why Claude Dojo, a poll of the room, the instructors, and the plan for both days. My part was a short introduction.

blocks.name: What changed in AI
blocks.what: The last twelve months of AI, how the job market now prices AI fluency, and use-case ideas from the room.

blocks.name: Install Claude Code
blocks.what: Hands-on. Everyone installed Claude Code, then ran a prompt that has Claude interview them to write a context file.

blocks.name: Fundamentals
blocks.what: How LLMs work, hallucination, model tiers, the four ways to use Claude, plans, tokens, and usage limits.

blocks.name: Fifteen terms, as a rap
blocks.what: The rap I made with Claude, then skills, plugins, and connectors, then the prompts that made the rap.

blocks.name: Build your first Skill
blocks.what: My job-search numbers, then a live run of the resume-tailoring Skill I use myself on a real job description. Then each person had Claude interview them into a Skill for a task they repeat, ran it, said what came out wrong, and ran it again.

blocks.name: Job search tools
blocks.what: Folder structure, daily job alerts, NotebookLM, referral blurbs, and battle cards.

blocks.name: Safety and ethics
blocks.what: Safety and a healthy skepticism, guardrails, and gray areas raised by the room.

blocks.name: Prompting, and agents as a preview
blocks.what: A prompting framework, being interviewed by Claude, dictation, and screenshots. Then MCP, plan mode, goal loops, the context window, and agent fleets, shown as a preview.

blocks.name: Connect an MCP
blocks.what: Hands-on: connecting the Canva MCP server to Claude, so it can reach an app outside the terminal.

blocks.name: Capstone kickoff
blocks.what: Build a tool that proves you can do the job. Pick a real task from your own work and have Claude make mock data for it, so nothing blocks you that evening.

blocks.name: Evening build, by room
blocks.what: Everyone started their capstone in plan mode, in rooms by track, including a coding room and a finance room. My run sheet had me leading the beginner room, which promised no code and no jargon.

blocks.name: Job search panel
blocks.what: From my run sheet, which had me hosting: guests on what their searches were like and what recruiters see, closing on referrals over volume.

blocks.name: Engineering track
blocks.what: Prompts for day-to-day engineering work, planning and building a feature with agents, and interviewing in the AI era.

blocks.name: Polish and ship
blocks.what: From my run sheet: finish the capstone and make it shareable, then write one paragraph: the task, what you built, the result.

blocks.name: Wrap-up
blocks.what: What comes next: the belt ladder, certifications, and demo groups.
